doc.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015

title: Kate Smith Show staff job at NBC after Vaughan Monroe
summary: After the Monroe band broke up, Bucky got an NBC staff job on the Kate Smith Show through a cellist; he talks pay and security, and never wanting to do anything else.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: But what about also, let’s say, the prospects of being a musician. Are you going to be able to make a good living. Was that an issue?
Well you had to be with a big band to get a little work.
Okay so that was 1940—
About ’51.
I was finished with the big band. Vaughan broke up then. I went back to New York and luckily I got a job as a staff musician playing for the “Kate Smith Show.”
So what network was that on?
NBC.
Wow. How did you get that?

We did a radio show with Vaughan Monroe and we had violins just for the show. And I met one of the cello players on the street and he said to me — Brownie, his name was Brown — he said, “they’re looking for a guitar player at NBC. Tell them I sent you up.” And I used his name and I got the job without auditioning or anything. And I did it for a whole year, her last year on television.
And you were expected to be able to sight read, chords and —
Yeah. A little solo here and there.
Do you remember what that paid?
$250 a week.
That’s not bad.
That was good then.
Five days a week?
Five days a week. Whether you were there or not.
Whether you were there or not?
Well if you had a day off or a week off, if you went to California, you still got paid as a staff musician.
All right. And meanwhile you have a growing family, right?
Yeah.
So were there tough years financially?
No I don’t think so, not with that kind of a gig. That solved all of the problems.
That’s nice.
We never fought over money. We were very happy.
Did you ever have a moment in your life, from the time of Vaughan Monroe on, where you felt I have to do something else?
No. I always wanted to play the guitar and that was it. And I never thought of any other thing. I couldn’t do anything else but play the guitar.
